purpose: Test whether latent predictive pretraining improves recovery of hidden physical parameters from partial dynamical observations without changing or reinterpreting any prior LAM-JEPA result.
research_question: Does a JEPA-style latent predictor learn representations that make latent physical parameters more identifiable than reconstruction-first or randomly initialized representations under the same data and probe budget?

hypotheses.primary: A frozen JEPA encoder will reduce median normalized parameter-estimation error by at least 10% relative to a matched reconstruction autoencoder on the held-out parameter grid.
secondary: The JEPA representation will retain its advantage when 25% and 50% of observations are masked.
A linear probe on frozen JEPA embeddings will outperform a linear probe on random features, showing that any gain is present in representation geometry rather than only end-to-end adaptation.

data_contract.generator: deterministic numerical simulation with stored configuration and seed
data_contract.split_rule: Split by parameter combinations, not by trajectory frames, so test physics is genuinely unseen.

methods.candidate: Context encoder + target encoder + latent predictor trained to predict masked future/held-out state embeddings; target encoder updated by EMA; no pixel/state reconstruction term in the primary candidate.
baselines: supervised end-to-end parameter regressor with the same encoder capacity
methods.probe: Linear probe on frozen pooled embeddings for each hidden parameter; one fixed MLP probe is allowed only as a declared secondary analysis.

metrics.primary: median normalized absolute parameter error averaged across hidden parameters
secondary: Spearman correlation between latent distances and parameter distances

success_gate.primary_pass: At least 10% relative reduction in primary error versus the autoencoder baseline on the untouched test split and no collapse diagnostic failure.
success_gate.strong_pass: Primary pass plus positive effect in both physical systems and at least two of three observation regimes.
success_gate.failure: Anything else is recorded as negative/inconclusive without changing this gate.

compute_gate.phase_1: Single-system small-width smoke run with one seed.
compute_gate.phase_2: Only after phase_1 correctness: full declared systems and seed set.
compute_gate.seed_policy: Choose and record seeds before phase_2; never discard completed seeds based on outcome.

related_2026_motivation: Physics-informed JEPA work has moved physical consistency into latent predictive states.
Recent latent-space parameter-calibration work reports that reconstruction accuracy alone is insufficient for inverse problems.
This protocol tests the narrower falsifiable question of parameter identifiability from JEPA embeddings.
